To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cyclic hypoxia is a unique stimulus for endothelial and tumor cell adaptation, which leads to a selective induction of COX-2 and that this enzyme largely accounts for the specific phenotype of endothelial cells and tumor cells exposed cyclically to low oxygen levels.

cyclic hypoxia, which is a feature of many solid tumors, induces COX-2 expression in tumor and endothelial cells and that COX- 2 is required for the increased angiogenic and metastatic potential of tumor cells exposed to fluctuating pO2.
cyclic hypoxia, a hallmark of tumors and of tumor blood vessels, leads to the selective induction of PTGS2/ COX-2 in both tumor cells and endothelial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new targets for the treatment of tumors with high levels of hypoxia.
the identification of genes that are selectively induced by cyclic (fluctuating) hypoxia in tumor endothelial and tumor cell lines.
the identification and characterization of new genes that are induced by hypoxia in tumor cells and endothelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cyclic hypoxia, which is the most frequent form of tumor hypoxia, is associated with a different transcriptomic signature than continuous hypoxia.
the cyclic hypoxia–induced gene signature of endothelial and cancer cells includes PTGS2/ COX-2.
cyclic hypoxia is associated with a unique gene signature, including COX-2, which may be of clinical relevance in the context of tumor progression and angiogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified COX-2 as a major actor of the transcriptomic adaptation of endothelial and cancer cells to cyclic hypoxias.
we have shown that the hypoxia-inducing factor (HIF)-1α–dependent gene program of endothelial cells is modified when they are exposed to cyclic hypoxic conditions.
COX-1/2 is an HIF-1 target gene and is upregulated by cyclic hypoxa.
The main takeaway from our work is that

cyclic hypoxia induces the expression of COX-2 in endothelial and tumor cell lines, and that COX- 2 accounts for the higher survival of endothelial cells, as well as the higher metastatic take in tumor cells.

cyclic hypoxia, which mimics tumor hypoxia in vivo, is a potent inducer of cyclooxygenases in endothelial and tumor cell populations, which in turn confers a survival and metastatic advantage to these cells.
cyclic hypoxia, which is characterized by alternating periods of hypoxia and reoxygenation, is associated with an increase in the expression of COX-2, which is not observed under continuous hypoxia.
